From Middle High German strō, from Old High German strō. Cognate with Old Norse strá, Old English streaw, Dutch stro, English straw.

s:
1787 CE: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, Egmont
Ich sehe kein Mittel, weder strenges noch gelindes, dem Übel zu steuern.
I see no means, neither severe nor mild, by which to stem the evil.
streng.et: From Middle High German strenge, from Old High German strengi (“strong”), strangi, from Proto-Germanic *strangijaz (“tight, tense”), *strangaz, from Proto-Indo-European *strengʰ- (“taut”); related to Proto-Indo-European *ster- (“stiff”). Cognate with Dutch str…

s: Da rauchen sie dann Haschisch ... aber das ist streng geheim.
There they smoke hashish ... but that is strictly secret.
streng.et: From Middle High German strenge, from Old High German strengi (“strong”), strangi, from Proto-Germanic *strangijaz (“tight, tense”), *strangaz, from Proto-Indo-European *strengʰ- (“taut”); related to Proto-Indo-European *ster- (“stiff”). Cognate with Dutch str…

Strang.et: From Middle High German strank, stranc, strange, from Old High German stranc, from Proto-Germanic *strangiz, from Proto-Indo-European *strengʰ-; related to Middle High German strange f, from Old High German stranga (“strand”). Cognate with Low German Strenge, …

s: Sie blies sich eine Strähne ihres schwarzen Haares aus der Stirn.
She blew a strand of her black hair from her forehead.
streak (of a liquid), bundle of rays (of light)
Strähne.et:
From Middle High German strëne, from Old High German strëno, from Proto-West Germanic *strenō, from Proto-Germanic *strinô (“strip, strand”), from Proto-Indo-European *ster- (“strip, line, streak”).
Cognate with Dutch streen and probably English strand. The sp…

Strauch.et: From northern Middle High German strūch, from Old High German *strūh, from Proto-West Germanic *strūk. Cognate with Dutch struik, Middle Low German strûk. Upper German originally lacked the word and some dialects still avoid it today.

s: Ich kaufte meiner Freundin einen Strauß Blumen.
I bought my girlfriend a bunch of flowers.
Strauß.et: Inherited from Middle High German, related to strotzen (“to teem with”), Icelandic strútur, Old Norse strútr.
Inherited from Middle High German strūȥ, strūȥe, from Old High German strūȥ, borrowed from Latin strūthiō, from Ancient Greek στρουθίων (strouthíōn).
From Middle High German strūȥ (“shrub, tuft”).

s: stroke (act of striking e.g. with a hand or a cutting weapon)
Streich.et: From Middle High German streich, from Old High German *streih, from Proto-West Germanic *straik (“stroke”). Compare Dutch streek, English stroke. In Middle High German the form strīch also occurs, which is either an adaptation to, or a new derivation from, the…

Streit.et: From Middle High German strīt, from Old High German strīt, from Proto-West Germanic *strīd, from Proto-Germanic *strīdaz.

s: at the end of the day
the direction to which hairs, or similar things, are inclined
Katzen muss man mit dem Strich streicheln.
